Photograph: Eric Lee/Reuters Donald Trump FAA investigates air ‘safety incident’ involving Trump’s Marine One Controllers allegedly failed to halt flights, leading to a ‘loss of separation’ with a departing passenger jet Richard Luscombe and agencies Wed 5 Aug 2026 08.58 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 08.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An air “safety incident” in which Donald Trump ’s Marine One helicopter came closer than permitted to another aircraft over Washington DC is under investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Air traffic controllers are believed to have mistakenly failed to halt commercial flights at Ronald Reagan national airport in northern Virginia on Tuesday afternoon when the military helicopter lifted off from the White House with the president on board. A “loss of separation” incident occurred in which the helicopter and a recently departed passenger jet bound for Florida came closer to each other than regulations allow, a source told Reuters. The aircraft are not believed to have been on a collision course. The FAA said in a statement that it was “investigating a safety incident involving Marine One but it didn’t appear to be a dangerous close call and the aircraft weren’t apparently converging”. The episode followed a tightening of proximity rules in the wake of a January 2025 collision between a commercial airliner and an army Black Hawk helicopter over the nation’s capital that killed 67 people. The government eventually admitted negligence in what was the deadliest crash on US soil in more than two decades. The aircraft involved in Tuesday’s incident was an Embraer E170 jet operated by Envoy ​Air, a wholly owned subsidiary of American Airlines, as flight 3742 to Pensacola. Tracking website Flightaware showed it left its gate at Reagan national at 2.18pm on Tuesday, 34 minutes later than scheduled, and was in the air 16 minutes later at 2.34pm. Marine One took off from the Ellipse near the White House at 2.33pm to take Trump to Joint Base Andrews and a flight to Los Angeles, according to a pool report. FAA rules implemented after last year’s tragedy require aircraft to remain separated by at least ​1.5 miles horizontally and 500ft vertically around airports, and the sources told Reuters that it appeared Marine One and the plane did ​not maintain separation. One said it appears they were not converging during the incident. Marine One and the Envoy jet continued their journeys without incident, with the Embraer landing in Pensacola at 3.33pm CT after a flight of 2hr 16min. The Guardian has contacted the White House and American Airlines for comment. Reuters ‌learned from its sources, who were speaking under the condition of anonymity, that the FAA planned to convene a safety review team to investigate the incident. A third aircraft, regional flight Republic 4700 from North Carolina’s Raleigh-Durham international airport to Washington DC, was three miles (5 km) from Reagan national at the time of the incident and was ordered to fly around before landing at 2.52pm, one of the sources said, confirmed by Flightaware tracking . The FAA ⁠imposed permanent restrictions on helicopter operations around Reagan national following last year’s mid-air collision. The US government conceded in December in a response to a lawsuit filed by one of the victims’ families that failures of the FAA and army played a role in the crash. “The United States admits that it owed a duty of care to plaintiffs, which it breached, thereby proximately causing the tragic accident,” it said. The ​National Transportation Safety Board said in January that a series of systemic failures by the FAA led ​to the collision, ⁠citing its decision to allow helicopters to travel close to the airport with no safeguards to separate them from airplanes. The FAA has since banned mixed helicopter and jet traffic around the airport, and commercial traffic is typically halted when Marine One is in flight around ⁠the airport. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/15/scho.text: At least 27 pupils and a teacher were killed on Thursday after a roof collapsed at a school in the northwest Pakistani city of Peshawar, a hospital official said.Asim Khan from Peshawar's Lady Reading Hospital confirmed the toll to the AFP news agency, adding that over 30 people were injured, with six believed to be in a critical condition.A spokesperson for the emergency rescue service in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province said the schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way."When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed on to another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside," spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said."There are concerns that more children may still be trapped beneath the rubble," he said, adding that 16 ambulances, two disaster response vehicles and more than 60 personnel were deployed to the site.Images released by the emergency services showed rescue workers in high-vis vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.Resident Sher Ahmed said he blamed "substandard construction materials" for the tragedy, and called for a probe."With profound grief and sorrow, I urge the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and take strict action against anyone found responsible so that such tragedies can be prevented in the future," he said.'Deep sorrow'Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in a statement expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives"."The Prime Minister extends his condolences to the bereaved families and prays for them to have the strength and patience to bear this irreparable loss," the statement said.President Asif Ali Zardari branded the roof collapse a "heartbreaking tragedy"."In this hour of grief, the entire nation shares the sorrow of the affected families," he said in a statement.Roof and building collapses are common across Pakistan, mainly because of poor safety standards and shoddy construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.In June this year more than a dozen children were killed in a roof collapse at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-storey building collapsed in the impoverished area of Lyari in the southern city of Karachi.
